claims.text: A multimap approach combining targeted free-energy perturbation (TFEP) and on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling (OPES) is the proposed intervention.
The proposed multimap/TFEP/OPES approach can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The cost reduction would arise from improved convergence of free-energy estimates.
Configurational mapping strategies are the structural or computational mediator of the intervention.
Enhanced sampling improves the convergence of free-energy estimates.
The proposed approach reduces training overhead.
The approach will predict fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties faster than explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
The approach will predict fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties more accurately than explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
The proposed method is intended for high-temperature conditions.
The proposed method is intended for high-pressure conditions.
The stated composition boundary is elemental and binary systems.
The stated temperature boundary is an unspecified high-temperature range.
The effectiveness of the proposed approach for multicomponent high-entropy systems is uncertain.
A benchmark comparing free-energy differences and computational cost against explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD can test the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain a significant improvement in both computational cost and accuracy relative to the baseline methods would falsify the hypothesis.
